take_homes: Default to one agent. Split only for access, dialect or stance. Ask 'could one prompt do this?' before paying for more.
Handoffs between agents are where numbers get lost, and nothing in the process checks whether the final briefing is true.
An agent that touches other systems needs approval, a stop condition and a worst-case question before I let it near finance data.

monday.move: Ask IT what it would take to approve one agent on finance data, read-only. Hold the month-end variance commentary until then.
monday.who: me, then IT and my controller
monday.when: this week, an email, not a project
monday.stop_condition: IT says no, or nobody can give me a monthly cost for 40 users
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: The module teaches how to design and split agents, which does read as something a team builds. But it never gives a cost, a payback or a licence comparison, so I still think of AI as a tool I buy and the hiring and building language as jargon. The 'one agent unless you can show why' slides came closest to shaking it.

one_line: Useful rule hidden in the middle: use one agent unless you can prove you need more. But I spent ninety minutes and never saw a cost or an answer I could verify.
